drivingQuestion: When the wind covered the blood, does the obligation to cover it survive, and does it revive if the blood is uncovered again?
outcomeNote: Rav Pappa's principle answers the difficulty and is left standing.

segments.he: כִּסָּהוּ הָרוּחַ. אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁחָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה, אֲבָל לֹא חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה – פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת. וְכִי חָזַר וְנִתְגַּלָּה מַאי הָוֵי? הָא אִידְּחִי לֵיהּ! אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: זֹאת אוֹמֶרֶת אֵין דִּיחוּי אֵצֶל מִצְוֹת.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if «the wind» blew earth on the blood and «covered it» one is obligated to cover the blood. «Rabba bar bar Ḥana says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: They taught» this halakha «only» if the blood «was again uncovered. But» if the blood «was not again uncovered» one is «exempt from» the obligation «to cover it.» The Gemara asks: «And when» the blood «was again uncovered, what of it? Isn’t it» already «rejected» from the mitzva of covering since it was covered by the wind? «Rav Pappa said: That is to say» that «there is no permanent» rejection «with regard to mitzvot.» Although the wind covered the blood, the mitzva to cover it was not rendered null; rather, the mitzva simply could not be performed. Consequently, once the blood is again uncovered, the mitzva to cover the blood remains in place.

moves.summary: The gemara quotes the mishna's clause about blood the wind covered.
moves.about: quoting the mishna's clause that if the wind covered the blood one is obligated to cover it

moves.cueHe: אמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן: לא שנו אלא
moves.summary: Rabbi Yohanan restricts the obligation to where the blood became uncovered again.
moves.about: narrowing the mishna's obligation to cover wind-covered blood to where the blood was afterwards uncovered again

moves.summary: The gemara objects that the mitzva was already discharged when the wind covered the blood.
moves.about: if the wind's covering already discharged the mitzva, re-exposure of the blood should not revive the obligation

moves.summary: Rav Pappa answers that there is no rejection with regard to mitzvot, so the duty stands.
moves.about: answering that there is no permanent rejection with regard to mitzvot, so the duty revives when the blood is uncovered
